rendered.description: M12 phase F: closed-loop following with the head camera rendered in the loop (bipe.m12.rendered_link)
rendered.status: Phase F plan approved by the user (22 October 2026), implementation in progress
rendered.pose_conversion_basis: As phase C: the tag pose is turned into range and bearing with the plant's own camera pose (lean and pitch included), as if the Pi knew it. 'fixed_mount' (the camera of the robot standing level at the nominal posture) is the diagnostic for a Pi that is not told the lean

nominal.basis: The phase C scene as rendered: the M10 plant's spot light (bipe.m10.plant) and the M12 directional light (bipe.m12.scenarios.world_xml), with the 200 lx noise budget (config/perception-m12.json camera.noise)

dim.basis: The phase C dim comparison, 50 lx (camera.noise.low_light_lux). Auto exposure and gain bring white to the same level under the 10 ms exposure cap, so dim light shows as sensor noise, not a darker image

side_light.basis: Assumption: a strong low light from one side (a window), about 20 degrees above the horizon, with the spot and headlight turned down to little fill; the tag face is lit unevenly and the floor brightly. Matte paper and ink, no specular glare (the phase C materials)

rendered.basis: User decisions (22 October 2026, phase F plan approved as recommended): run phase F before phase E with the phase C camera pose and timing estimate; latency drawn from the phase C Pi Zero 2 W estimate by tracker mode; 5 nominal seeds (the renders are deterministic, so seeds vary only latency and sensor noise); dim and strong side light on three scenarios
rendered.lights_order: The scene's lights in model order: the M10 plant's spot light, then the M12 directional light

follower.description: M12 phase D following controller: the target estimator, the mode logic and the follower law that run in the supervised Teensy core (firmware/src/follower.c, Python reference bipe/m12/follow.py), and the measurement link model that stands in for the Pi (bipe/m12/pi_model.py). tools/generate_follower_config.py writes firmware/include/follower_config.h from this file. SI units; angles in radians unless the name says degrees.
follower.status: Phase D, for the user's sign-off at the phase exit

timing.basis: The follower steps with the balance core at 200 Hz (config/robot.json simulation.control_dt). The pose history covers 0.5 s, which holds the 0.26-0.34 s re-acquisition latency (artifacts/m12/perception/timing.json) with margin; a measurement older than that is rejected. The link delay is the phase C latency budget's 2 ms (an assumption until phase E). Frames arrive at 30 Hz (phase C sign-off).

camera.basis: Head camera at the nominal 40 degree posture, pitched 42 degrees for the waist tag (bipe.m12.geometry.camera_pose; config/following-m12.json tag.layouts.waist_tag). Body lean from the balanced equilibrium moves the camera along the body: 0.0647 m at -4 degrees, 0.0830 m at +4 degrees, so 0.1311 m/rad (central difference; 0.0550 and 0.0916 m at -8 and +8 degrees, within 1 mm of the line). Each pose in the history carries the camera position at its lean, so the lean is not read as target motion (the first closed-loop runs without it held a 2 Hz, +-8 degree pitch oscillation: the +-1.8 cm camera motion entered the target velocity estimate and the speed command). The follower law holds the range from the upright camera, a fixed point on the robot

noise_table.basis: The phase C measurement model (config/perception-m12.json measurement_model.table): at each range, the largest standard deviation over view angles up to 60 degrees; linear in range, held at the ends

estimator.noise_basis: The rendered-frame spreads are a floor (phase C: lens calibration, levelling error, rolling shutter, ISP and real light are not in them), so the filter uses three times the table with floors of 1 cm and 0.25 degree. The range bias is not corrected (phase D decision 1, 21 October 2026)
estimator.process_basis: Constant-velocity target in the robot's odometry frame with white acceleration noise; the density is tuned in the open-loop tests (artifacts/m12/following/open_loop) against the target's 1.0 m/s^2 acceleration requirement

gating.basis: While following, a detection is accepted when its innovation is inside the 99.99 % bound of the filter (chi-square, 2 degrees of freedom) or within the 0.3 m reacquisition gate; while coasting or braking only the 0.3 m gate applies (config/following-m12.json reacquisition.gate_m)

modes.basis: config/following-m12.json engage, loss and reacquisition rules (phase A sign-off) and the phase A ideal follower: engage after 5 consecutive detections over at least 0.15 s at 0.5-1.5 m with the robot at rest, and only after an explicit follow request (phase D decision 2); coast on the prediction from 2.25 frame periods without an accepted detection (the phase A 1.5 frame periods plus the 25 ms spread of the tracking latency, which spaces the arrivals of successive reports by up to 58 ms); brake after the coast; a link silent for the coast time is a loss; hold once the commands are zero and the robot is below 0.05 m/s. Coast and stale link (phase D sign-off, user decision 22 October 2026): a flat 0.45 s, lengthened from 0.3 s so that it outlasts the 0.26-0.34 s full-frame search after a miss (artifacts/m12/perception/timing.json; phase D lost the target in 90 degree corners and 1 m curves for longer than the 0.3 s coast while the tracker searched, and the search sends no report). The user accepted the longer stop: from 1.0 m/s, 0.45 m coasting plus 0.5 m braking (config/following-m12.json loss.stopping_distance_max_m)

law.basis: The phase A ideal follower (config/following-m12.json ideal_follower, range, close_range): speed from the target's speed along the line of sight plus the range error; yaw rate from the bearing plus the target's speed across the line of sight; no forward speed below the 0.4 m stop range

limits.basis: The signed-off drive envelope (config/robot.json m10.targets.drive_envelope, phases A and B); reverse and brake are follower limits

link_model.basis: Phase C, signed off 21 October 2026 (artifacts/m12/perception/timing.json and summary.json): region-of-interest tracking with frames over 2 cores at 30 Hz; after a miss the next frame is a full-frame search at quad_decimate 2 on 4 threads; the frames whose image is ready before the search ends are skipped (the search ends at its latency less the 58.2 ms of half exposure, readout, ISP and link in the phase C latency budget); the latency of each frame is drawn uniformly from the estimate's range; after a missed frame the next is missed with at least the replays' 1 in 3. Detection probability, bias and noise come from the measurement model at the true range and view angle, with the yaw-blur term at the true bearing rate. The target starts its track 1 s after the robot (as the phase B replays) and the follow request arrives at 0.5 s

output.basis: The 2304 x 1296 sensor mode (2 x 2 binned, full field, up to 56 fps) scaled to half by the ISP into a 1152 x 648 stream, so one output pixel spans 4 x 4 native 1.4 um pixels; 30 Hz is the phase A assumption under test

render.basis: Render pixels per output pixel at the image centre; the remap filters the render to the output pitch, so edges and tag cells are resolved from a finer image than the output

blur.basis: Pixel aperture: a one-pixel box has a standard deviation of 1/sqrt(12) = 0.29 px. Lens and ISP scaler: an assumed 0.5 px Gaussian (the f/2.2 diffraction spot, 1.22 lambda N = 1.5 um, is a quarter of the 5.6 um output pixel; the rest stands for lens aberration and the scaler's filter). Depth of field: with focus at 1 m the hyperfocal distance is about 1.2 m (f^2 / (N c), c = 2 native pixels), so 0.5-2 m stays within a few native pixels of blur, under one output pixel; defocus is not modelled

exposure.shutter: global (sub-frame mean); rolling shutter is a later option
exposure.basis: The exposure is capped at 10 ms through the libcamera exposure limits so that motion blur stays bounded at the following yaw rates; analogue gain makes up the brightness at indoor light. Five sub-frames over 10 ms sample the motion every 2 ms (at 1.4 rad/s, 0.16 degree, under one output pixel at the image centre). 5 and 20 ms are compared in the blur set

noise.basis: Light: 200 lx on the tag, ordinary indoor room lighting (homes 100-300 lx, offices to 500 lx); 50 lx is the dim comparison. Photons: 1 lx at 555 nm is 1/683 W/m^2, or 4.1e15 photons/s/m^2 (the fewest photons per lux of any visible light, so conservative). Camera equation for a Lambertian scene: sensor illuminance = E R T / (4 N^2). QE 0.3: luminance-weighted quantum efficiency through the colour filters (IMX708 QE is not published; typical back-illuminated sensors peak near 0.7 before the colour filter). Read noise 2 e- per native pixel (typical of current 1.4 um back-illuminated sensors; not published for the IMX708), summed in quadrature over the 16 native pixels of an output pixel. White level: auto exposure puts a perfect white diffuser at 85 % of linear full scale before the sRGB tone curve; ISP denoising and sharpening are not modelled. All assumptions until real footage exists
